correctness.rationale: The periodic hat Gram matrix equals (4I+S+S^{-1})/(6n) for \(n\ge3\). The infinite Green row with u=-2+sqrt(3) satisfies the Kronecker recurrence and periodizes to the exact inverse. A nodal kernel is linear on each mesh arc, so its L1 norm is exactly six times the stated H-sum. Convexity makes nodal evaluation globally maximal and the kernel sign is a sharp input. Infinite Green absolute mass is exactly 2; periodization gives the strict finite upper bound and the universal 4q^m error upper estimate. For even/odd n, two period images have rigorously opposite signs on fixed-width windows with explicit lower masses, proving a positive c_* q^m defect. Taking nth roots yields the sharp limit. check.py separately reconstructs 26 inverse rows in exact rationals, performs 1,722 finite assertions, and matches exact small n values. No finite computation is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: This solves the natural finite-size endpoint robustness question for periodic lowest-order spline least-squares projection on a standard uniform mesh, directly relevant to the stability coefficient in near-best approximation. Earlier theory bounds arbitrary partitions by 3 and periodic ones uniformly without exact constants, while the infinite uniform mesh has norm 2. The theorem identifies the strict finite periodic improvement, a computable exact constant at every n, and the optimal exponential speed of convergence of that improvement (not just an algorithmic recomputation of the full-line limit). The input and output norms, object, and optimal rate are mathematically natural, and the lower bound needs a sign-cancellation argument not supplied by the known general stability bounds.
